title: Ex-Post Value for Money (VfM) Analysis in US Highway Projects
content: Public-private partnerships (P3s) have become an increasingly adopted delivery method for major U.S. highway infrastructure, with Value for Money (VfM) analysis serving as the primary analytical basis for procurement decisions. VfM assessments compare the estimated cost of conventional public delivery against the risk-adjusted cost of private delivery to determine the preferred pro-curement approach. While VfM analysis has been well-established at the procurement stage, no published peer-reviewed study has examined whether these estimates remain consistent with outcomes observed after project completion. This study addresses that gap by reconstructing pro-curement-stage and post-completion VfM values for seven completed U.S. highway projects using the FHWA P3-VALUE toolkit as a standardized analytical framework, with post-completion values updated using realized project data while maintaining a consistent model structure and discount rate. A Wilcoxon signed-rank test was applied to assess whether systematic differences existed between paired estimates. The Wilcoxon signed-rank test did not detect a statistically significant difference between procurement-stage and post-completion VfM estimates (exact two-sided p = 0.6875). VfM increased in three projects and decreased in four, while all seven projects retained their original directional VfM conclusions when the available post-completion information was incor-porated. However, the small sample size and limited statistical power mean that the non-significant result does not establish equivalence or demonstrate the general stability of procurement-stage VfM assessments.
